newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait plans $330 million firm to create jobs.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait plans $330 million firm to create jobs.

text.p: Kuwait said on Tuesday it planned to form a 100 million dinar ($330 million) firm to finance jobs for Kuwaitis in the private sector.
Planning Minister Ali al-Zmei'a announced the plan during a parliament session discussing unemployment among Kuwaitis, the official Kuwait News Agency reported.
The government, which provides a cradle-to-grave welfare system for its 720,000 nationals, employs 92.7 percent of the Kuwaitis in the workforce.
Wages and salaries absorb about half of the $14 billion annual state budget while experts say hidden unemployment among Kuwaitis is about 50 percent.

The new company "is part of several steps by the government to encourage the employment of Kuwaitis in the private sector as part of implementing the economic reform plan in a scientific manner which does not ignore the social aspects", Zmei'a was quoted as saying.
Training courses in various fields were also planned, he added.

KUNA gave no further details about the new company. MPs have voiced concern over the fate of Kuwaiti employees in the next stage of privatisation, when utility firms whose services are heavily subsidised and are used as employment centres are to be sold off.
The government has presented a draft law to parliament to move to the next stage of privatisation which could lead of layoffs and higher prices for basic services.

Officials say the draft law contains many ideas to tackle the unemployment and price of basic services concerns, insisting that funds earned from privatisation and Kuwait's oil wealth were sufficient to pay for generous redundancies and training to retool the Kuwaiti workforce.

Proposed solutions include offering to pay part of the salaries of Kuwaitis employed by privatised strategic services firms on a decreasing annual scale over several years, experts said. The state could also grant citizens cash to cushion the rise in prices.
Since the start of the first phase of the privatisation plan in September 1994, Kuwait has sold stakes in 20 local firms for $2.3 billion. About 34 other firms worth some $3 billion remain.
